Computed R1 dissipation under the stated exercise condition (48 V on /IN, /OUT clamped to 0 V) analytically and confirmed with an ngspice-42 .op simulation.

Independently rebuilt board connectivity from the saved file in pcbnew 10.0.7 (saved zone fill, no refill): 0 unconnected items; pad nets match schematic; verified clamp current path J1.1 -> 0.25 mm F.Cu track -> R1 -> /OUT tracks -> J1.2.

findings.mechanism: R1 connects /IN (pin 1) directly to /OUT (pin 2) per the verified netlist and board pads. With /OUT clamped to 0 V off-board, the full 48 V appears across the 10 kOhm resistor: I = 4.8 mA, P = V^2/R = 48^2/10000 = 0.2304 W. This is 230% of the stated 0.1 W continuous limit, applied indefinitely, so R1 operates in sustained overload for the entire clamp duration; C1 carries no DC and provides no relief. The ngspice operating point confirms 4.8 mA and 0.2304 W dissipated in R1. The sole stated evaluation criterion is therefore failed with a 130% margin exceedance; meeting 0.1 W at 48 V would require R1 >= 23.04 kOhm.
findings.reasoning: This is the single criterion the exercise asks to evaluate, and it fails deterministically by direct calculation from the native schematic value and verified connectivity, independently confirmed by simulation. The overload is continuous (clamp held indefinitely) and large (2.3x), not a marginal or transient exceedance, so the fitted R1 cannot sustain the specified condition. Severity blocking because the design as saved cannot meet the only stated requirement; the allegation is fully supported by calculation and the stated limit, with no unstated ratings imposed.
findings.title: R1 dissipates 230.4 mW continuously under the specified 48 V / clamped-output condition, 2.3x its stated 0.1 W limit

findings.mechanism: ERC, DRC, netlist and the geometry probe verify rule compliance, parity and connectivity only; none applies the 48 V stimulus or computes component dissipation. The design fails the stated criterion (finding PHY-1) despite a fully clean check record, so the check suite as composed provides no coverage of the one requirement under evaluation. A reader aggregating outcomes ('pass, pass, info, info') without an explicit power/stress check could wrongly conclude the candidate meets the exercise requirement.
findings.reasoning: Flagged per the instruction to independently challenge verification coverage. A successful exit of every native check is not proof of electrical behavior; here the clean record coexists with a blocking electrical defect. Info severity because it is a coverage observation about the verification record, not an additional flaw in the board itself.
findings.title: Packet verification suite does not exercise the stated electrical criterion; all-pass toolchain results must not be read as electrical qualification

limitations: R1 power limit (0.1 W) is taken as given by inputs/requirements.txt; no part model or datasheet exists in the candidate to independently confirm the fitted part's rating.
Board connectivity evaluated against the saved zone fill; the read-only candidate forbids a refill pass, so fill-state-dependent connectivity was verified as saved only.
No thermal simulation of R1 on the 0805 footprint was performed; time-to-failure or steady-state temperature under the 2.3x overload was not quantified, only the limit exceedance itself.
